steps.body: To compare decimals, line up the places: compare tenths digits first, and only check hundredths when the tenths tie.
steps.narration: To compare decimals, line up the places: compare tenths digits first, and only check hundredths when the tenths tie.

widget.prompt: Shade the grid to show 0.35. Each full column is one tenth; each cell is one hundredth.

commonCounts.feedback: That shades 0.50 — the OTHER number in the comparison. Shade 0.35: three full columns and five cells.

widget.successFeedback: Three columns and five cells — 0.35. Against 0.5's five full columns, the grid shows 0.5 covers more.
widget.lowFeedback: The shaded amount is still below the target. Fill whole columns for the tenths digit first, then single cells for the hundredths.
widget.highFeedback: The shaded amount has gone past the target. Each full column is one tenth — check the tenths digit before adding single cells.

predict.reveal: 0.5 is 5 tenths — five full columns. 0.35 is only 3 full columns and 5 cells. The tenths digits decide it: 5 > 3, so 0.5 is greater even though 0.35 has more digits.

cml.actionGoal: Manipulate the model and track how it represents g4d compare.
invariants: The manipulated model and the mathematical relationship for g4d compare must stay consistent.
misconceptions: Changing a visible feature without preserving the relationship that defines g4d compare.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: What change would make the model stop representing the same mathematical relationship?

explanationVariants: Compare tenths first: the amounts differ, so 0.5 > 0.35.

widget.prompt: Compare the two decimals: 0.5 ? 0.35. Choose the relation that holds.
widget.successFeedback: Correct — comparing digit by digit from the tenths place settles it: 0.5 > 0.35.
widget.ltFeedback: Line up the places before deciding: compare the tenths digits of 0.5 and 0.35 first, and only look at hundredths when the tenths tie. Counting digits instead of comparing places points the wrong way here.
widget.eqFeedback: These two decimals name different amounts. Compare place by place — the digits differ, so the two values cannot be equal.

steps.body: More digits does not mean more value: 0.5 beats 0.35, because 5 tenths beats 3 tenths before hundredths are even read.
steps.narration: More digits does not mean more value: 0.5 beats 0.35, because 5 tenths beats 3 tenths before hundredths are even read.
